title: One record per unit: who holds a phase, what it cost, was it reviewed, is anyone working (gh-503)
body:
Closes #503. Closes #499. Closes #496. Closes #500. Closes #501. Closes #430. Closes #518.

> **Draft — do not merge yet.** See the Ready checklist at the bottom.

## What this PR became, and why

It began as #503 — *"nothing records which agent holds a phase."* It now carries **two specs, two
plans (13 phases), three folded-in branches and seven issues**, because on 2026-09-20 five
sessions worked one seam in parallel — *what the orchestrator intends versus what actually
happened to a dispatched unit* — and gave it five specs. The cost of that split is recorded in the
second spec's §1 and §8: two discarded implementations, **two different `schema_version: 3`s of
the same artifact**, two refusals for one issue, and a live data-loss bug. The operator's call was
to land the seam whole.

| folded in | what it carried | state |
|---|---|---|
| gh#519 `fix/fr-run-cursor-cluster` | #496 manual phases, a second #499 refusal, #500 session binding, #501 composite ids | merged `228d784`, PR closed as superseded |
| gh#517 `feat/journal-require-reviews` | #430 `fr journal check --require-reviews` | merged `85b1c92`, PR closed as superseded |
| `main` ×2 | gh#506 (tier ingestion — which had independently fixed two of this PR's own findings), gh#514 (telemetry, handoff bounds) | merged |

## The investigation #503 asked for

Eight `fr-phase-executor`s were dispatched; ten hours later the harness listed two, one of them
long since returned and still resumable with no worktree. **Nothing about the dispatch differed,
and nothing was reaped.** All eight are still fully recorded on disk, identical in dispatch shape.
The listing is a view over agents that are *not yet terminal*.

One never became terminal. Claude Code moves a foreground `Bash` call past its **120-second
timeout** into a background child; five of eight executors were promoted that way, none by choice.
One of them left behind an `until grep … ; do sleep 3; done` loop watching a file for a pattern
that never appeared. It ran **11.5 hours**. One live background child is the whole asymmetry —
neither the devcontainer nor fr-isolation is implicated — and killing the child did *not* retire
the agent, which is why a holder record needs its own explicit close.

## What ships

**One record per unit.** `StepRecord.units` replaces `items`, `dispatch` and top-level
`accounting`. Each unit holds its **attempts**, oldest first; each attempt carries who held it,
which session dispatched it, what it was estimated to cost and what it measurably burned.

| surface | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `fr run advance` | opens an attempt; **refuses** a held unit (exit 2, no brief, names the holder); `--redispatch` is the escape |
| `fr run claim` | **new** — records the reported agent id; `--abandoned` closes an attempt without resolving its step |
| `fr run resolve` | closes the attempt and measures it; a `review-phase` unit **refuses `done` without `--evidence review=<journal-entry-id>`** |
| `fr run status` | per attempt: holder, then estimate, then measurement — labelled as different quantities |
| `fr run check` | open and unclaimed dispatches, pre-gate reviews as debt; **`--idle` exits 3** on an advanceable run nobody is working; `--stalled-after` reports, never fails |
| Stop hook (Claude Code) | blocks ending a turn on an idle run and names the next command; silent for every legitimate stop; fail-open; once per cursor position |
| OpenCode plugin | continues the session on `session.idle` — weaker than blocking, and declared `partial` |
| `run` artifact | **v2 → v5** across this PR; the last hop is the first *body-rewriting* run migration |

`fr` cannot verify any *reported* field — the orchestrator says which agent it dispatched, exactly
as `--answered-by operator` says a human answered. Visibility, not enforcement.

### Verified on the run that built it

```
phase/3/implement-phase: done
  agent a6003d67… (claude-code, claude-fable-5-1) 21:04:30 -> 22:02:04 done
    ~23,599 tok est
    measured: 56,092,764 tok billed across the dispatch's turns
```

Identity and cost on one attempt — the split #464 and #503 had left between them. The evidence
gate was verified *by meeting it*: no evidence → exit 2; a `finding` id → exit 2; another phase's
review → exit 2; this phase's own → `done`, with the cursor byte-identical after the refusals. The
cursor migrated v4 → v5 **while holding an open attempt**: held before, held and still named after.

## Findings — 25 across two plan journals, none open

`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-dispatch-holder-identity --section findings`
`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-unit-record-unification --section findings`

Nearly every one is the same shape — **a claim that outran the code**:

| | the claim | the reality |
|---|---|---|
| f2 | the validator item had passing tests | it produced no code; two open records for one unit parsed cleanly |
| f3 | the notification said `exit code 0` | the suite was red — a pipeline exits with `tail`'s status |
| f4 + f6 | `model` = "the resolved tier binding" | `from_phase` is a sentinel **and** `fr plan create` silently dropped every `tier:` — `null` on every real dispatch (gh#506 fixed both independently, and better; its code is what ships) |
| f7 | `dispatch` held the holder history | `_complete_step` deleted a grouped step's whole map the moment it finished |
| f11 | three tests asserted a concrete `model` | reading the harness from the ambient machine — green here, red on CI |
| f13 | `run` was at `schema_version: 3` | so was gh#514's branch, for a different shape; nothing detects two branches allocating one number |
| f-p2-blind-grep | the plan's exit-criterion grep passed | `git grep -E` has no `\b`; it could not match anything, so it could not fail |
| p3 | synthesized attempts + "held iff last attempt open" | **jointly wrong**: every pre-#508 unit of every migrated cursor read as HELD |

**Executors refuted the orchestrator's spec four times, with evidence, and were upheld each
time** — the synthesized-attempt hold above (30 synthesized attempts on real captures, zero wrongly
held after the fix); "a `phase/<n>` key is always `manual`" (a captured v1 cursor says otherwise);
a second design conflict between gh#508 and gh#519 the orchestrator had not listed; and two facts
only the Claude Code binary could supply (`background_tasks`, and a built-in cap on Stop-hook blocks).

A recurring sub-theme, fixed each time and now in shipped guidance: **a verification that cannot
fail is not one.** A masked exit code, an inert `set -e`, a grep that matches nothing, a mutation
that never applied, a `$` that was an anchor — every one read as a pass. Mutation checks now print
whether they applied, and the new tripwire carries its own positive control.

## Operator gates

Run `2026-09-20-feat-phase-holder-identity` (captured before its cursor drifted — gh#517's new
`journal-check` step means `fr run gates` now refuses this completed run, by design):

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

Run `2026-09-20-unit-record-unification-r2`, verbatim:

```
brainstorm: cleared, but provenance not recorded (this cursor predates `answered_by`)
```

That second line is an artefact of **adoption**, which cannot carry provenance; the wording
("predates") is not quite the truth. For the record: the operator answered four question batches
for that spec (nine questions — scope, the gh#519 fold-in, and decisions `u1`–`u5`), reviewed the spec
over four rounds, and approved the plan. Its first cursor was stranded by manifest drift mid-run and
re-adopted; the dispatch history lost in that recovery is preserved in the plan journal.

## Operator review — two comments, both acted on

**"is this valid yaml?"** (a cursor's `stdout: 'self-review passed` folded over three lines).
Valid — three ways — but it looked broken, and a failed step's output rendered as one escaped
blob. `fr.run.model.dump_cursor_yaml` is now the ONE cursor writer; multi-line strings are block
literals, round trip exact (18 awkward strings pinned), no schema change. Widening the
writer-agreement test to every captured cursor then found something nobody asked about: the
4→5 rewrite ordered `synthesized` ahead of the cost fields, so **every migrated cursor would
have reordered itself on its first native save.** Fixed in `v4_to_v5`, mutation-checked.

**"I would expect another element here, invoking `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. Is it
being left at the implementing agent's discretion?"** It was — and this run proves it: every
phase was reviewed inline, with neither review skill invoked through the harness. Decision
`u6` (spec §4.E.1): `skill:` takes an ordered list and the member names both; and
`evidence: [review, findings]`, where **`findings` is derived, never passed** — `resolve
--state done` refuses while any finding filed against that phase is still open, prints the
`fr journal resolve` line for each, and records the ids it saw closed. Deferral is a phase
number, not a new state. Deliberately **not** a third member step: drift compares member ids,
and a new one strands every `fr-goal` cursor in flight. Five mutations each fail the suite;
disabling the gate fails the shipped-shape walk. **Limit:** it enforces that findings *end
closed*, not that the review was rigorous or a refutation well reasoned.

## Acceptance

**36 rows added since `origin/main`** (the 36th, `run-review-findings-gate`, by the operator review below), grouped in the second spec's §7 by what could go wrong:
upgrade safety, the witness, cost, evidence, liveness. Repo total: `ci: 146, skipped: 18,
not-implemented: 7`. Three rows of this PR stay `not-implemented` **on purpose** — each is
live-only by nature:

- `run-dispatch-harness-neutral` — two different harnesses writing one record shape; a fixture
  only shows that fr writes what fr writes.
- `run-pickup-on-another-host` — its unit half landed; its claim is two real machines.
- `run-idle-reprompt-opencode` — all 50 `bun` tests drive a fake client.

gh#519's `run-advance-refuses-running` is merged into `run-dispatch-refuses-second` by notes on
both rows (there is no delete verb); both stay `ci`.

## Limits and costs, stated

- **The idle guard only reaches session-bound runs**, calls the `fr` on PATH (a stale global `fr`
  exits 2 and *silently disables it*), and adds ~2 s to each turn end of a bound session.
- **Hermes has no adapter** — there, fr-goal's prose is all there is. OpenCode's is `partial`.
  Codex and Copilot CLI are `unsupported` across the matrix; their block-capable stop hooks are
  noted as leads, unverified except that Copilot CLI's hooks system is installed.
- **Not exercised:** the Stop hook delivered through a plugin's `hooks.json`, `background_tasks`
  while a subagent really runs, interactive sessions — Test Plan item 17. The plugin's TypeScript
  is tested (`bun test`) but was not type-checked.
- **Known wrinkle, not fixed here:** session bindings say `harness: "claude"` where `fr.harness`
  says `"claude-code"`. The guard keys on `worktree` only.

## On upgrade

Only the `run` kind moves. A cursor migrates at the first `fr` command (an agent runs
`fr migrate artifacts --yes` itself — standing behaviour). Held units stay held and named; recorded
cost moves onto the last attempt; cost older than the dispatch record gets a **synthesized**
attempt that is never a hold. Reviews resolved before the evidence gate read `done, unevidenced` —
debt, never a failure — while reviews still to come need evidence. A cursor that cannot be
converted is left byte-identical. Everything under `implemented/` stays frozen; the new frozen
legacy reader can still parse an archived cursor on demand.

## Verification

Full suite as CI sees it (`CLAUDE*` unset): **3966 passed, 80 skipped, 0 failed**, coverage
**92.21%**. `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy` (146 files), `bump-version --check`
(**4.12.0**), `fr acceptance check` + `report --check`, `fr validate artifacts` (48),
`fr harness parity --check`, both mirror generators, `fr workflow check fr-goal`,
`fr journal check --require-reviews` on both plans, `bun test` (50) — all clean. Explainer
renderer verified byte-identical on the unmodified source before the real render.

## Test Plan — post-merge, operator-driven

**Post-merge, operator-driven (decision d4) — both harnesses:**

13. A live `/fr-goal` run on **Claude Code**: `fr run status` during a phase shows that phase
    held by the real subagent id, and after it returns shows the dispatched→returned pair with
    `harness: claude-code` and the tier's model. Transcript in the PR.
14. The same on **OpenCode**, recording `harness: opencode` and the child session id, proving
    the record is harness-neutral rather than Claude-shaped.
15. On one of those runs, deliberately `advance` twice for the same phase and confirm the
    refusal fires with the real holder id — the #499 behaviour, live.

**Post-merge, operator-driven** (extends #508's items 13–15):

16. On the live Claude Code run of item 13: `fr run status` shows cost **under each
    attempt**, and after a deliberate `claim --abandoned` + re-dispatch, both attempts'
    costs are present.
17. End a turn mid-run with the run idle: the Stop hook blocks and names `fr run advance`.
    End one while an executor works: it does not.
18. Try to resolve a `review-phase` unit `done` with no review entry: refused.
## Process finding — recorded, not designed

Five sessions, one seam, no shared view. Two cheap guards would have prevented most of this PR's
reconciliation work: **batch issues that name the same structure into one spec**, and a
**registry-side check that two open branches have not allocated the same artifact version**.
Neither is built here; both are why the second spec exists.

---

- [ ] Explicit review approval
- [ ] No commits pushed since that approval
